```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Zhao_2026_nivolumab_ccrcc"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70481> (open access, PMC13599598)
* Supporting information: Data S1 (Tables S1-S8, Figures S1-S6 and the
  model-development text with the full model equations).

Nivolumab is a fully human IgG4 monoclonal antibody against PD-1. Its
subcutaneous formulation is co-formulated with recombinant human
hyaluronidase PH20 (rHuPH20). The phase III trial CheckMate 67T
(NCT04810078) compared subcutaneous nivolumab 1200 mg every 4 weeks
(Q4W) with intravenous nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks (Q2W) in patients
with previously treated advanced or metastatic clear-cell renal cell
carcinoma (ccRCC). Its co-primary PK endpoints, the time-averaged
concentration over the first 28 days (`Cavgd28`) and the steady-state
trough (`Cminss`), were derived from a population PK model rather than
from noncompartmental analysis.

The paper fits the model in two stages, and both are packaged here:

| Model | Stage | Data | Parameter table |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Zhao_2026_nivolumab_pooled` | Stage 1, pre-specified pooled model | historical intravenous nivolumab monotherapy studies plus subcutaneous CheckMate 8KX | Table S4 |
| `Zhao_2026_nivolumab_ccrcc` | Stage 2, CheckMate 67T model | CheckMate 67T only, with the Stage 1 estimates entering through NONMEM `$PRIOR` | Table S5 |

The Stage 2 model is the one the paper used to derive the individual
exposures for the non-inferiority test and to bridge to the alternative
600 mg Q2W and 900 mg Q3W subcutaneous regimens, so most of this article
uses it. Both models share one structure: two compartments, zero-order
intravenous infusion into the central compartment, first-order
absorption from the subcutaneous depot with a logit-scale bioavailability,
and clearance that declines over time as a sigmoid function of time since
the first dose.

The paper's third component -- bridging to other solid-tumour indications
-- re-used earlier indication-specific intravenous popPK models with the
Stage 2 `ka` and `F` added. Those indication models are not reported in
the paper and are not reproduced here; the published intravenous base
model they descend from is available as `Bajaj_2017_nivolumab`.

The pre-specified model of the companion methodology paper is packaged
separately as `Zhao_2025_nivolumab`. It has the same structure but a
different set of estimates (and two tumour-type effects on clearance), so
it is not the Stage 1 model of this paper.

```{r load-models}
mod_ccrcc <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Zhao_2026_nivolumab_ccrcc"))
mod_pooled <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Zhao_2026_nivolumab_pooled"))
```

# Population

```{r population, echo = FALSE}
pop <- mod_ccrcc$population
data.frame(
  Characteristic = c(
    "Patients (s.c. / i.v.)", "Age", "Baseline body weight",
    "Baseline eGFR", "Baseline albumin", "Female", "ECOG performance status",
    "Disease", "Dosing"
  ),
  Value = c(
    sprintf("%d (%d / %d)", pop$n_subjects, pop$n_subjects_sc, pop$n_subjects_iv),
    pop$age_range, pop$weight_range, pop$renal_function, pop$albumin,

    pop$disease_state, pop$dose_range
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "CheckMate 67T Stage 2 analysis population (Zhao 2026 Table 1).")
```

Race was 85.0% White, 12.5% other, 1.0% American Indian / Alaska Native,
0.8% Asian and 0.4% Black (Table 1). The Stage 1 dataset pooled 3540
patients over 20 studies (Table S2); its baseline demographics are not
reported.

# Source trace

Every Stage 2 value comes from Table S5 and every Stage 1 value from
Table S4 of Data S1. The equations come from the Data S1 section "Model
development". The source time unit is hours; `CL`, `Q` and `ka` are
multiplied by 24 and `T50` divided by 24 so that the packaged models run
in days.


# Virtual cohort

The cohort is drawn from the Table 1 marginal distributions of the
CheckMate 67T analysis population: body weight log-normal with mean 77.7
and SD 17.3 kg truncated to the observed 35-157 kg, eGFR normal with mean
63.7 and SD 19.9 mL/min/1.73 m^2 truncated to 20.7-124, 32.4% female and
60.8% with ECOG performance status of 1 or more. Covariates are drawn
independently because the joint distribution is not published. The same
200 subjects are simulated under every regimen with the same random-effect
seed, so regimen comparisons are paired.

```{r cohort}
n_sub <- 200L

set.seed(67)
wt_sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (17.3 / 77.7)^2))
wt_meanlog <- log(77.7) - wt_sdlog^2 / 2
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n_sub, wt_meanlog, wt_sdlog), 35), 157),
  CRCL = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_sub, 63.7, 19.9), 20.7), 124),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.324),
  ECOG_GE1 = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.608)
)
summary(cohort[, c("WT", "CRCL")])
c(female_pct = mean(cohort$SEXF) * 100, ecog_ge1_pct = mean(cohort$ECOG_GE1) * 100)
```

# Simulation of the CheckMate 67T and bridging regimens

Five regimens, matching Figure 2 and Tables S6 and S8: subcutaneous
1200 mg Q4W, 900 mg Q3W and 600 mg Q2W into the depot, and intravenous
3 mg/kg and 10 mg/kg Q2W as 30-minute infusions into the central
compartment (the CheckMate 67T infusion duration, Table S2). Following
Data S1, steady state is taken after 336 days of dosing (12 Q4W or 24 Q2W
doses), so the steady-state interval is the last dosing interval ending
on day 336.

The observation grid is fine over the first 28 days and the steady-state
interval, daily in between, and carries points just before each dose time
(a record exactly on a dose time is read after the dose) and at the end
of each infusion.

```{r simulate}
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,            ~amt,  ~per_kg, ~tau, ~cmt,      ~dur,
  "s.c. 1200 mg Q4W",    1200,  FALSE,   28,   "depot",   0,
  "s.c. 900 mg Q3W",      900,  FALSE,   21,   "depot",   0,
  "s.c. 600 mg Q2W",      600,  FALSE,   14,   "depot",   0,
  "i.v. 3 mg/kg Q2W",       3,  TRUE,    14,   "central", 0.5 / 24,
  "i.v. 10 mg/kg Q2W",     10,  TRUE,    14,   "central", 0.5 / 24
)
t_ss_end <- 336

build_events <- function(reg) {
  dose_times <- seq(0, t_ss_end, by = reg$tau)
  obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
    seq(0, 28, by = 0.25),
    seq(29, 196, by = 1),
    seq(t_ss_end - 28, t_ss_end, by = 0.25),
    dose_times[dose_times > 0] - 1e-4,
    if (reg$dur > 0) dose_times + reg$dur
  )))
  obs_times <- obs_times[obs_times <= t_ss_end]
  amt_i <- if (reg$per_kg) reg$amt * cohort$WT else rep(reg$amt, n_sub)
  dose <- data.frame(
    id = rep(cohort$id, each = length(dose_times)),
    time = rep(dose_times, n_sub),
    amt = rep(amt_i, each = length(dose_times)),
    evid = 1L,
    cmt = reg$cmt
  )
  dose$rate <- if (reg$dur > 0) dose$amt / reg$dur else 0
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = rep(cohort$id, each = length(obs_times)),
    time = rep(obs_times, n_sub),
    amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", rate = 0
  )
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

simulate_regimen <- function(mod, i) {
  reg <- regimens[i, ]
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod, build_events(reg), returnType = "data.frame", addDosing = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, Cc) |>
    dplyr::mutate(treatment = reg$treatment)
}

sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), \(i) simulate_regimen(mod_ccrcc, i)))
sim$treatment <- factor(sim$treatment, levels = regimens$treatment)
nrow(sim)
```

## Replicating Figure 2: geometric-mean profiles by regimen

```{r figure2, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2 of Zhao 2026: predicted geometric-mean nivolumab concentration-time profiles by regimen over the first 28 weeks."}
gm <- function(x) exp(mean(log(x)))

prof <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= 196) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(gmean = gm(pmax(Cc, 1e-6)), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(prof, aes(time / 7, gmean, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (week)", y = "Nivolumab concentration (ug/mL)", colour = "Dose"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The figure reproduces the published panel: the 10 mg/kg intravenous
regimen sits well above every subcutaneous regimen; the three
subcutaneous regimens converge on the same average concentration with
fluctuation that grows with the dosing interval; and 3 mg/kg intravenous
gives the lowest profile with the sharp infusion peaks that make it the
only regimen with a higher `Cmax1` than 600 mg subcutaneous Q2W.

# PKNCA validation against Tables S6 and S8

Each exposure measure is an NCA interval:

* `Cavg1`, `Cmax1` -- the first dosing interval `[0, tau]`;
* `Cavgd28` -- `[0, 28]`;
* `Cavgss`, `Cmaxss` -- the last dosing interval ending on day 336;
* troughs -- `Cmin1` (end of the first interval), `Cmind28` (day 28),
  `Cmind84` (day 84, the Table S8 comparison time point for the Q3W
  regimen) and `Cminss` (day 336) -- the minimum over the last day before
  that dose time. A trough window must not reach back to a dose time:
  over `[0, tau]` the minimum is the pre-dose zero, not the trough.

The paper summarises each measure as a geometric mean over subjects, so
the per-subject PKNCA results are reduced to geometric means before the
comparison (`ncaComparisonTable()` otherwise reduces by the median).

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = as.character(treatment))

dose_df <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  reg <- regimens[i, ]
  data.frame(
    id = cohort$id, time = 0, treatment = reg$treatment,
    dose = if (reg$per_kg) reg$amt * cohort$WT else reg$amt
  )
}))

trough_window <- function(trt, label, t_dose) {
  data.frame(treatment = trt, interval = label, start = t_dose - 1, end = t_dose - 1e-4,
             cmax = FALSE, cmin = TRUE, cav = FALSE)
}

intervals <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  reg <- regimens[i, ]
  tau <- reg$tau
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(treatment = reg$treatment, interval = "first", start = 0, end = tau,
               cmax = TRUE, cmin = FALSE, cav = TRUE),
    data.frame(treatment = reg$treatment, interval = "d28", start = 0, end = 28,
               cmax = FALSE, cmin = FALSE, cav = TRUE),
    data.frame(treatment = reg$treatment, interval = "ss", start = t_ss_end - tau, end = t_ss_end - 1e-4,
               cmax = TRUE, cmin = FALSE, cav = TRUE),
    trough_window(reg$treatment, "trough_1", tau),
    trough_window(reg$treatment, "trough_d28", 28),
    trough_window(reg$treatment, "trough_d84", 84),
    trough_window(reg$treatment, "trough_ss", t_ss_end)
  )
}))

measure_map <- tibble::tribble(
  ~interval,     ~PPTESTCD, ~measure,
  "first",       "cav",     "Cavg1",
  "first",       "cmax",    "Cmax1",
  "trough_1",    "cmin",    "Cmin1",
  "d28",         "cav",     "Cavgd28",
  "trough_d28",  "cmin",    "Cmind28",
  "trough_d84",  "cmin",    "Cmind84",
  "ss",          "cav",     "Cavgss",
  "ss",          "cmax",    "Cmaxss",
  "trough_ss",   "cmin",    "Cminss"
)

# For Q4W the first dosing interval and the 28-day window coincide, so one
# PKNCA interval can feed two measures (Cavg1 and Cavgd28): map measures to
# (treatment, start, end, parameter) and give PKNCA each window only once.
interval_measures <- intervals |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(cmax, cmin, cav), names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "requested") |>
  dplyr::filter(requested) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(measure_map, by = c("interval", "PPTESTCD")) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, start, end, PPTESTCD, measure)

intervals_pknca <- intervals |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, start, end) |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(c(cmax, cmin, cav), any), .groups = "drop") |>
  as.data.frame()

o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, dose ~ time | treatment + id)
o_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose, intervals = intervals_pknca))

nca_res <- as.data.frame(o_nca$result) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(interval_measures,
                    by = c("treatment", "start", "end", "PPTESTCD"),
                    relationship = "many-to-many")

sim_gm <- nca_res |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, measure) |>
  dplyr::summarise(gm = gm(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r reference}
# Zhao 2026 Table S6 (s.c. 1200 mg Q4W, s.c. 600 mg Q2W, i.v. 3 and
# 10 mg/kg Q2W) and Table S8 (s.c. 900 mg Q3W and the day-84 trough);
# geometric means in ug/mL.
ref_gm <- tibble::tribble(
  ~measure,  ~`s.c. 1200 mg Q4W`, ~`s.c. 900 mg Q3W`, ~`s.c. 600 mg Q2W`, ~`i.v. 3 mg/kg Q2W`, ~`i.v. 10 mg/kg Q2W`,
  "Cavg1",    78.8,  63.9,  45.0,  29.8,  99.3,
  "Cmax1",    108,   81.3,  54.2,  63.6,  212,
  "Cmin1",    50.8,  49.0,  41.9,  19.6,  65.5,
  "Cavgd28",  78.8,  NA,    62.0,  37.7,  126,
  "Cmind28",  50.8,  NA,    68.1,  31.9,  106,
  "Cmind84",  94.1,  107,   122,   NA,    NA,
  "Cavgss",   182,   182,   182,   92.5,  308,
  "Cmaxss",   230,   214,   199,   138,   461,
  "Cminss",   126,   141,   157,   71.5,  238
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-measure, names_to = "treatment", values_to = "ref") |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(ref))

cmp <- dplyr::inner_join(ref_gm, sim_gm, by = c("treatment", "measure")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pct_diff = (gm - ref) / ref * 100,
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = regimens$treatment),
    measure = factor(measure, levels = measure_map$measure)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(treatment, measure)

cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    ref = signif(ref, 3), gm = signif(gm, 3),
    pct_diff = sprintf("%+.1f%s", pct_diff, ifelse(abs(pct_diff) > 20, "*", ""))
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = treatment,
    "NCA parameter" = measure,
    "Published GM (ug/mL)" = ref,
    "Simulated GM (ug/mL)" = gm,
    "% diff" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Geometric-mean exposures: simulated (200 virtual subjects per regimen) vs. Zhao 2026 Tables S6 and S8. * = more than 20% from the published value.")
```

```{r assert-exposures}
stopifnot(
  # A mis-transcribed clearance, volume, ka, F or unit conversion shifts
  # every exposure by tens of percent.
  abs(median(cmp$pct_diff)) < 10,
  quantile(abs(cmp$pct_diff), 0.9) < 20
)
```

Every published geometric mean in Tables S6 and S8 is reproduced to within
about 10%, with the simulated values running a few percent low across
all regimens alike. A uniform offset of that size is what a virtual
cohort drawn from independent marginals (rather than the trial's own
covariates and empirical Bayes estimates) is expected to give; it leaves
the regimen and route comparisons, which are ratios, unaffected.

```{r gmr}
gmr <- sim_gm |>
  dplyr::filter(measure %in% c("Cavgd28", "Cminss")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = gm) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    measure,
    `s.c. 1200 mg Q4W / i.v. 3 mg/kg Q2W` = `s.c. 1200 mg Q4W` / `i.v. 3 mg/kg Q2W`,
    `s.c. 600 mg Q2W / i.v. 3 mg/kg Q2W` = `s.c. 600 mg Q2W` / `i.v. 3 mg/kg Q2W`
  )
gmr |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-measure, \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Exposure" = measure) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated geometric-mean ratios, subcutaneous vs. 3 mg/kg intravenous.")
```

The paper reports a CheckMate 67T geometric-mean ratio (from the
individual Bayes estimates) of 2.098 for `Cavgd28` and 1.774 for `Cminss`
for 1200 mg subcutaneous Q4W vs. 3 mg/kg intravenous Q2W, and simulated
ratios of 1.64 and 2.20 for 600 mg subcutaneous Q2W (Table S7). Ratios
from Table S6 itself are 78.8 / 37.7 = 2.09 and 126 / 71.5 = 1.76.

```{r assert-gmr}
stopifnot(
  # Route comparison: subcutaneous exposure is roughly double the 3 mg/kg
  # intravenous exposure for both co-primary endpoints.
  all(gmr$`s.c. 1200 mg Q4W / i.v. 3 mg/kg Q2W` > 1.4),
  all(gmr$`s.c. 1200 mg Q4W / i.v. 3 mg/kg Q2W` < 2.8)
)
```

# Stage 1 vs. Stage 2

Typical-value profiles (random effects set to zero) for the reference
subject (80 kg, eGFR 90 mL/min/1.73 m^2, male, PS 0) show how little the
CheckMate 67T re-estimation moved the pooled model. The Stage 2
subcutaneous absorption is slightly slower and less complete (`ka` 0.295
vs. 0.310 /day, `F` 0.788 vs. 0.815) and the eGFR exponent on clearance
is larger (0.306 vs. 0.166). For the reference subject the two
intravenous profiles coincide (the disposition estimates differ by at most
a few percent), so the Stage 1 intravenous line is hidden under the
Stage 2 one.

```{r stage-compare, fig.cap = "Typical-value profiles of the Stage 1 (pooled) and Stage 2 (CheckMate 67T) models for the reference subject."}
ref_subject <- data.frame(id = 1L, WT = 80, CRCL = 90, SEXF = 0, ECOG_GE1 = 0)

typical <- function(mod, label, cmt, amt, tau, dur) {
  ev <- if (dur > 0) {
    rxode2::et(amt = amt, ii = tau, until = 168 - 1e-6, cmt = cmt, dur = dur)
  } else {
    rxode2::et(amt = amt, ii = tau, until = 168 - 1e-6, cmt = cmt)
  }
  ev <- rxode2::et(ev, seq(0, 168, by = 0.25), cmt = "central")
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev, ref_subject, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    dplyr::select(time, Cc) |>
    dplyr::mutate(model = label)
}

stage_cmp <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  typical(mod_pooled, "Stage 1 (pooled): s.c. 1200 mg Q4W", "depot", 1200, 28, 0),
  typical(mod_ccrcc, "Stage 2 (ccRCC): s.c. 1200 mg Q4W", "depot", 1200, 28, 0),
  typical(mod_pooled, "Stage 1 (pooled): i.v. 3 mg/kg Q2W", "central", 240, 14, 0.5 / 24),
  typical(mod_ccrcc, "Stage 2 (ccRCC): i.v. 3 mg/kg Q2W", "central", 240, 14, 0.5 / 24)
)

ggplot(stage_cmp, aes(time, Cc, colour = model)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (day)", y = "Nivolumab concentration (ug/mL)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Two models, one paper.** The Stage 1 pooled model (Table S4) and the
  Stage 2 CheckMate 67T model (Table S5) are separate fits to different
  datasets and are packaged as separate files. The Stage 2 model is the
  one the paper's exposures and bridging come from.
* **Reference body weight 80 kg.** Tables S4 and S5 and Figure S1 define
  the reference subject at 80 kg; the Data S1 equation legend says
  "WTB [75 kg]". The table value is used because it is the reference at
  which the printed estimates are defined, and it matches the control
  streams of the companion pre-specified model (`Zhao_2025_nivolumab`,
  `BBWT_R = 80`).
* **Additive IIV on EMAX.** Data S1 prints
  `Emax_i = Emax_REF + e^(eta_Emax,i)`. Read literally, a subject at
  `eta = 0` would have `Emax = -0.260 + 1 = 0.740`, a 2.1-fold *increase*
  in clearance over time, contradicting the reported decline. The
  exponent is taken as a typesetting slip for the additive form
  `Emax_i = Emax_REF + eta_Emax,i`, which is how the same group's control
  streams code it (`EMAX = AEMAX + ZEMAX`, `Zhao_2025_nivolumab`;
  `Bajaj_2017_nivolumab` Eq. 3). `cl_time_max` therefore stays on the
  linear scale (it is signed and carries an additive eta) and the
  convention check's "should be log-transformed" warning on it is
  expected.
* **No IIV on Q; no body-weight effect on Q or VP.** Data S1 lists Q among
  the parameters with IIV and says Q and VP are "expressed as a function
  of the WTB", but its printed equations are `Q_i = Q_REF` and
  `VP_i = VP_REF x e^(eta_VP,i)`, and neither table reports an omega for Q
  or a weight exponent on Q or VP. The equations and tables are followed.
  Table S4 Note 2 ("Between-subject variability in Q and VP and the
  covariance between Q and VP were fixed to the corresponding values as
  CL0 and VC") conflicts with the estimated `ZVP` in the same table and is
  not implemented.
* **Albumin not in the model.** The Data S1 CL0 equation includes a
  baseline-albumin power term, but the Data S1 list of final-model
  covariate effects omits it and neither table reports an albumin
  exponent. Albumin is documented in `covariatesDataExcluded` of the
  Stage 2 model.
* **Theta numbering gaps.** Table S4 numbers its fixed effects theta1-10,
  12-15, 17, 18, 26 and 27, and Table S5 theta1-16, 19 and 20. Table S5's
  gap (theta17-18) corresponds to the albumin slots of the generic
  equation; Table S4's gaps are not explained. The Table S4 reference
  subject lists no tumour type, so the Stage 1 model is taken to have no
  tumour-type effects (unlike `Zhao_2025_nivolumab`), and only the
  printed parameters are implemented.
* **`F1_PS` held at 1.00.** Both tables list a performance-status factor
  on bioavailability marked as not estimated with value 1.00. It is
  carried as `e_ecog_ge1_fdepot <- fixed(1)` so the provenance is kept;
  it has no effect.
* **Residual error is an SD.** The proportional residual error is reported
  as theta10 rather than as a sigma, i.e. as the proportional standard
  deviation (the companion control streams fix `$SIGMA 1` and multiply
  the prediction by this THETA).
* **Stage 1 study count.** The main text says Stage 1 pooled 17 historical
  intravenous studies with CheckMate 8KX; Table S2 lists 19 intravenous
  studies. The packaged population metadata sums Table S2.
* **Virtual cohort.** Covariates are drawn independently from the Table 1
  marginals; the paper used the observed CheckMate 67T covariates and
  empirical Bayes estimates, so exact agreement with Tables S6 and S8 is
  not expected.
* **Indication bridging not reproduced.** Figures 3 and 4 rely on earlier
  indication-specific intravenous popPK models that the paper does not
  report.
* No erratum to the paper was found (searched 2026-11-17).
